what_its_for: Trimipramine is used to treat depression. It belongs to a group of medicines called tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). It helps improve your mood, sleep, appetite, and energy levels, and reduces feelings of sadness and anxiety.
how_to_take: Take trimipramine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or glass of milk. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew it. Your doctor may have you take your full dose at bedtime since it can cause drowsiness.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 75 mg per day, which your doctor may slowly increase up to 150–200 mg per day depending on how you respond. Older adults usually start on a lower dose (around 50 mg per day). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store trimipramine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C–25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking trimipramine — it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may worsen side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid standing up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure. Limit time in the sun and use sunscreen, as trimipramine may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Tell your doctor before taking any other medicines, especially other antidepressants, cold or allergy medicines, or sleep aids.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or suicide (especially in the first few weeks), chest pain or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, difficulty urinating, seizures, signs of a severe allergic reaction (rash, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing), or confusion and agitation. Also contact your doctor if you feel your depression is getting worse or if you have unusual mood or behavior changes.
when_it_works: Trimipramine may start to improve your sleep and appetite within the first 1–2 weeks. However, it usually takes 2–4 weeks — and sometimes up to 6–8 weeks — before you feel the full benefit on your mood. Be patient and keep taking it as prescribed, even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with extra caution. Older patients are more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, falls, confusion, and heart rhythm changes. A lower starting dose is usually recommended. Children and teenagers: This medicine is generally not recommended for people under 18 years old. If prescribed to a young person, they should be watched closely for any worsening depression or thoughts of self-harm, especially in the early weeks of treatment. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Heart conditions: Use with caution if you have a history of heart disease or irregular heartbeat. Your doctor may want to monitor your heart with an EKG.
